Train a graph

Source: R/train.R
zl_trainer.Rd

zl_trainer() prepares a graph with a loss for training with an optimiser: it checks that every operation between a parameter and the loss has a gradient (zulm_unsupported_backward names the one that has not, and the call that made it), and builds the gradient and optimiser graphs once, through 'ggml-opt'. Every f32 parameter the loss depends on is trained; half-precision parameters cannot be.

Usage

zl_trainer(g, opt, accumulate = 1L, clip_norm = NULL)

zl_step(tr, data, lr = NULL)

zl_grad(tr, name)

zl_reset(tr)

Arguments

g

A graph from zl_graph() with a loss.

opt

An optimiser from zl_adamw() or zl_sgd().

accumulate

The number of batches whose gradients are summed before each update.

clip_norm

NULL, or the largest joint L2 norm of the gradients at an update.

tr

A trainer.

data

A named list of arrays for the graph's inputs, as for zl_forward().

lr

The learning rate of this step; NULL for the optimiser's.

name

A parameter's name.

Value

zl_trainer() returns a trainer; zl_step() the loss, a number; zl_grad() an array of the parameter's dimensions; zl_reset() the trainer, invisibly.

Details

zl_step() writes a batch into the graph's inputs, computes the loss and the gradients, and, every accumulate calls, updates the parameters. It returns the loss of the batch; a loss that is not finite gives a zulm_nonfinite_warning. With clip_norm, each update first scales all gradients together so that their joint L2 norm is at most clip_norm.

zl_grad() returns the gradient of the loss with respect to one parameter, at the parameters' current values, on the inputs last written by zl_step() or zl_forward(). zl_reset() zeroes the optimiser's state (AdamW's moments and step count).

An optimiser's state is not saved by zl_save(), and if a step is interrupted the state is undefined: call zl_reset() before going on.

Examples

p <- zl_params()
zl_param(p, "w", c(3, 1), init = zl_init_zeros())
g <- zl_graph(
  function(x) list(loss = zl_mse(zl_crossprod(zl_param_tensor(p, "w"), x$x), x$y)),
  p,
  inputs = list(x = c(3, 8), y = c(1, 8)),
  loss = "loss"
)
tr <- zl_trainer(g, zl_adamw(lr = 0.05))
set.seed(1)
x <- matrix(rnorm(24), 3, 8)
y <- matrix(c(1, -2, 0.5) %*% x, 1, 8)
for (i in 1:200) loss <- zl_step(tr, list(x = x, y = y))
loss
#> [1] 3.528795e-09
zl_param_get(p, "w")
#>            [,1]
#> [1,]  0.9999790
#> [2,] -1.9999368
#> [3,]  0.5000194
